entry_point: library API: Jsoup.clean / Jsoup.isValid and Cleaner.clean(Document) / Cleaner.isValid(Document) / Cleaner.isValidBodyHtml over untrusted HTML with a Safelist

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit: Jsoup.clean and Cleaner.clean(Document) over input containing a start tag whose written name has a trailing control character (U+0001, U+000B, U+001E, U+001F; lower, upper and attribute-bearing forms) resolve the element to an allowed opaque-text tag, swallow the rest of the input, and emit the swallowed markup verbatim; the emitted string carries an <svg onload=...> element the safelist does not allow. Also reproduced through Cleaner.clean on a preserve-case-parsed document and inside body, table, template and noscript-island contexts.
sites: src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/TagSet.java:140 - published-fix site: the registry trims a token-supplied name before lookup
src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/Token.java:302,315,390 - published-fix site: the token producers record a trimmed normal name
src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:592 - injected sibling S1: body start-tag dispatch re-normalises the token name before the tag lookup and the opaque-text decision
src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/HtmlTreeBuilder.java:196 - injected sibling S2: the noscript-island path re-normalises the token name before the tag lookup and the opaque-text decision
verified.routes: No Pattern B uncovered route: an exhaustive local sweep (8 opaque/RCDATA tag names x 26 control characters x 9 input shapes x 11 document contexts, plus Cleaner-on-document and preserve-case parsing) found no residual sanitizer bypass on the published fix alone. All residual routes are the injected siblings below.
injected_siblings: S1 src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:592 - the body start-tag default branch (where custom and opaque tags are resolved) rewrites the start token's name with the parse settings' tag normaliser before computing the text state and inserting the element

S2 src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/HtmlTreeBuilder.java:196 - insertNoscriptStartTag rewrites the start token's name with the parse settings' tag normaliser before the text-state decision and insertion
verified.services: none; offline after the image build
verified.project_tests_run: org.jsoup.safety.CleanerTest, org.jsoup.parser.TagSetTest, org.jsoup.parser.HtmlTreeBuilderTest, org.jsoup.parser.TokeniserStateTest, org.jsoup.safety.SafelistTest - 108 tests, all pass on the pinned+injected tree and on the oracle. org.jsoup.parser.HtmlParserTest is deliberately excluded: its trimNormalizeElementNamesInBuilder asserts the pre-fix trimming of control characters out of element names, which a correct fix must change (the published fix replaces that test).
verified.end_to_end: Separate-container simulation with the built env and verifier images: nop = 14/14 security failing, 120/120 functional passing, reward 0; oracle = 14/14 security + 120/120 functional, reward 1.0; every listed check patch behaved as declared.

patch_checks.note: T1: oracle with only the token-producer side changed; the registry still trims token names, so body content of disguised opaque tags is emitted raw
T2: oracle minus the body start-tag re-normalisation sibling; every body route stays open
T3: oracle minus the noscript-island start-tag re-normalisation sibling; the island route stays open
refuse_all: escapes every opaque element's content, so allowed raw content no longer round-trips
adjacent_api: removes trimming from the public tag-set lookup, changing its documented behaviour
oracle plus a defensive skip of any opaque content whose element name carries a control character; still 1.0
second valid design: trim the token name at production time so end detection and tag lookup always see the same name

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: clean has no error status; a fix that throws on attacker input is counted as a failing security case, so it cannot reach reward 1.0.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorization decision over a neighbouring or proxy object; the property is about the sanitized markup itself.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles or directions exist; the base route and each sibling route are enforced by separate tests rather than a single toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sanitizer only reads a document and returns markup; there is no separate write path to guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the sanitizer consults no external authority, so there is no fail-open-on-missing-answer mode.

traps.lever: base flaw / published-fix producer+registry split (pattern A)
traps.shape: start tag whose written name carries a trailing control character: the token producer records a trimmed normal name while the tokeniser keeps the untrimmed name for raw-text end detection, so the element resolves to an allowed opaque tag and the swallowed markup is copied verbatim. Shapes: lower/upper case, U+0001/U+000B/U+001E/U+001F, attribute-bearing, body/table/template contexts, Cleaner-on-document and preserve-case parse entry points.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the registry's trim is documented public-API normalisation and the pinned project test asserts it; the tempting fixes patch only the producer, only the registry, or escape every opaque DataNode in the sanitizer, and each of those either leaves the bypass open or breaks legitimate content.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified published-fix site; the advisory and the fix commit both centre on it

traps.lever: injected sibling S1 - body start-tag re-normalisation
traps.shape: same disguised names, but the token name is rewritten by the body start-tag dispatch before the tag lookup and the opaque-text decision; reaches ordinary body, table and template content and survives a producer+registry fix.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is one line in the giant start-tag state machine and reads as ordinary normalisation; after fixing the token producer a solver treats recorded names as authoritative and does not re-check the tree builder. It is behaviour-preserving for every ordinary name, so nothing in normal use reveals it.
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer normalising custom start-tag names before resolving them in the body dispatcher; indistinguishable from the surrounding code for every normal name

traps.lever: injected sibling S2 - noscript-island start-tag re-normalisation
traps.shape: disguised names inside a noscript island; the island path rewrites the token name before the text-state decision and insertion, and the sanitizer drops the unsupported noscript element while still copying its allowed children out.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the island path is recent, niche code and Safelist refuses noscript outright, so the route looks irrelevant even though allowed children of a dropped noscript element are copied to the output.
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer normalising names for the plain-markup island path; behaviour-preserving for every ordinary name and placed in code the published fix never touches
